mem.t: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

lessons.title: The Faithfulness of God
lessons.theme: God’s faithfulness is new every morning; he never breaks his word

v: It is because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail.
They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
If we are faithless, he remains faithful; for he can’t deny himself.”

lessons.still: Look out of the window at the sky, and remember that this morning the sun rose just as it always does. Quietly say, “Lord, great is your faithfulness.” Then recall three moments in the past year when God did not abandon you, and thank him for each one in turn.
teach: The sunrise is never late, and it never needs us to remind it. When Jeremiah wrote Lamentations, Jerusalem had just been burned and the temple lay in ruins. Yet there, among the rubble, he wrote: “They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.” His world had collapsed, but God had not.

Faithfulness here means that God keeps his word and keeps his covenant. Paul goes further: “If we are faithless, he remains faithful.” God’s faithfulness does not rest on our performance but on his own nature — “he can’t deny himself.” Our faithfulness runs hot and cold; his stands like a rock.

In the original language, the fruit of the Spirit called “faithfulness” is the same word as “faith.” We can be faithful to others because we have first experienced God’s faithfulness to us. A change of mindset: not “I must try hard to become a reliable person,” but “I stand on the God who is utterly reliable, and his faithfulness flows out through me.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard — God’s word never fails, and it is the surest foundation for life. Self-ruled people trust only themselves, and so they are often let down by themselves; people living the self-emptied life lean on the faithful God, and so they become people others can lean on.
q: Who is God? — When you were at your lowest, how did God show you his faithfulness?
Who am I? — Do you assume that God’s faithfulness depends on how well you perform?
How shall I respond? — For which act of God’s faithfulness will you give thanks today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus is called the one who is “Faithful and True” (Revelation 19:11). He said he would rise on the third day, and on the third day he rose from the dead; he promised to send the Counselor, and at Pentecost the Holy Spirit came. Peter denied him three times, yet Jesus held fast to his love and called Peter again by the lakeshore.
lessons.pray: Faithful God, thank you that your loving kindness never ends and your mercies are new every morning. Even when I am faithless, you remain faithful. Help me to live within your faithfulness, and let your faithfulness flow out through me, so that I become a blessing people can rely on. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three things God has promised and faithfully done in your life
Tomorrow, make your first words on waking: “Lord, great is your faithfulness.”
Share with one of “my 2” a time when God was faithful to you
lessons.noon: “They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.” — Lord, right now I lean on your faithfulness.

lessons.title: Faithful in Little Things
lessons.theme: Faithfulness in big things begins with the smallest things

v: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

lessons.still: List the small things you need to do today: reply to a message, arrive on time for an appointment, clear the dishes, finish a report. Place the list before the Lord and say, “Lord, in these small things too, I want to be faithful to you.”
teach: When a building collapses, it is often not because of one great earthquake but because, years earlier, a worker left out a few steel bars — “nobody will ever see it anyway.” Life is like that. Failure in big things usually grows out of compromise in small things, and faithfulness in big things is built up, little by little, in small things.

Jesus said, “He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.” What God values is not the size of the task but the direction of the heart. We often think, “Once I have more time, more money, more influence, I’ll really use it for the Lord.” But Jesus says that if we have not been faithful in small matters like “unrighteous mammon,” who will entrust us with the “true riches”?

Small things are God’s training ground. Being on time, keeping your word, doing your own job well, never taking a cent that isn’t yours — these may seem trivial, but they are the foundations of character. A change of mindset: nothing is “too small to matter,” because everything is done before the Lord.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and you change your life; change your life and you change your lifestyle. The fruit of faithfulness is not produced on the platform but in the details of daily life. Letting Jesus reign includes letting him reign over every small thing I do.
q: Who is God? — God cares about even the smallest things — what does that show you about him?
Who am I? — In which “small things” do you often tell yourself, “This doesn’t matter”?
How shall I respond? — In which small thing will you be faithful to the Lord today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus spent many years as a carpenter in Nazareth, and Scripture records almost nothing of those years. Yet before he began his public ministry, the Father said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.” That pleasure included his ordinary, faithful days in the carpenter’s workshop.
lessons.pray: Lord, forgive me for so often despising small things and wanting only to do big ones. I am willing to be faithful to you in the smallest things: being on time, keeping my word, being honest, and doing well every task that is mine. In these ordinary days, produce in me the fruit of faithfulness. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Be on time for every appointment today; if you will be late, let people know in advance
Fulfil one small promise you have been putting off
Follow through for one of “my 2” on a small thing you once casually promised
lessons.noon: “He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.” — Lord, right now I will be faithful to you in this small thing.

lessons.title: The Faithfulness of Daniel
lessons.theme: We stay faithful under pressure because our hearts already belong to God

v: Then the presidents and the local governors sought to find occasion against Daniel as touching the kingdom; but they could find no occasion or fault, because he was faithful. There wasn’t any error or fault found in him.

When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.

lessons.still: Like Daniel, find a quiet corner. Kneel, or sit with your head bowed. Picture your window opening toward God’s presence. Don’t rush to speak; begin with thanks: “Lord, just as I always do, I come before you.”
teach: Only when the storm comes can you tell which tree has deep roots. Daniel served as an official in Babylon for decades, through more than one dynasty. His enemies wanted something to use against him and combed through all his affairs, yet “they could find no occasion or fault, because he was faithful.” In the end, the only place they could attack him was his faith.

Notice the words “as he did before.” When the decree was issued, Daniel didn’t change. He didn’t suddenly become brave; his everyday habit of praying three times a day had long since rooted his heart in God. His faithfulness at work and his faithfulness in prayer were two sides of one life: faithful to God, and therefore faithful to people.

When a crisis comes, we don’t suddenly rise to our ideals; we fall back to the level of our everyday habits. That is why today’s “as before” matters so much. Everyday prayer, everyday honesty, everyday diligence are the foundation that will let us stand firm in the future. Faithfulness is lived out one day at a time.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships — first with God, then with myself, then with others, then with things. Because Daniel’s relationship with God was secure, he could be faithful before people and in his work. His focus was on God, not on his circumstances, and not even a den of lions could change him.
q: Who is God? — God shut the lions’ mouths in the den — what does that show you about him?
Who am I? — What is your “as before”? When pressure comes, which habits will you fall back on?
How shall I respond? — Which “just as before” spiritual habit will you build?
lessons.jesus: On the night he faced the cross, Jesus still went out “as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives” to pray (Luke 22:39). His faithfulness was not a moment of heroism but the natural fruit of a lifetime of communion with the Father. On that darkest night he said, “Not my will, but yours, be done.”
lessons.pray: Lord, make me like Daniel, rooted in you in ordinary days. Whether at work, at home, or in church, let no one find grounds to charge me with unfaithfulness. When pressure comes, help me to stay faithful to you, just as I always have. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Set a regular daily time for prayer, and begin today
At work, do one task well that no one will ever check
Every day at a set time, pray for one of “my 2”
lessons.noon: “And prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.” — Lord, right now I come before you, just as I always do.

lessons.title: Entrusted According to Ability
lessons.theme: The Lord looks not at how much, but at faithfulness

v: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’
“His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

lessons.still: Quietly ask yourself: what has the Lord entrusted to me? Time, health, skills, family, money, a job… Hold them one by one in the palm of your hand, the way a steward holds his master’s property, and say, “Lord, all of this is yours.”
teach: A steward lives in his master’s house and manages his master’s money, yet he knows full well that none of it is his. In the parable of the talents, the master entrusts different amounts “each according to his own ability”: one receives five talents, one two, one one. The amounts differ, but the responsibility is the same: faithfulness.

Notice that the servant with two talents receives exactly the same praise, word for word, as the one with five: “Well done, good and faithful servant.” The master does not grade on the size of the result but on faithfulness. The servant with one talent failed not because he received little but because he was afraid — he saw his master as a hard man, so he buried the money in the ground.

Wrong ideas about God make us afraid to take risks and unwilling to give. The fruit of faithfulness grows from a right knowledge of our Master: he is good, and he entrusts things to us because he trusts us. A change of mindset: from “I have only a little; it doesn’t matter” to “The Lord has given me this little, and I will be faithful with it.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: It is required of stewards that they be found faithful. Self-ruled people treat their gifts as their own assets — they either show them off or bury them. People living the self-emptied life know that everything belongs to the Lord, and they want only for their Master to receive the greatest glory. The glory is not mine; it belongs to Jesus.
q: Who is God? — The master gave both servants the same praise — what does that show you about God?
Who am I? — Because you feel you have “little ability,” have you buried your gifts?
How shall I respond? — Which talent the Lord has entrusted to you will you bring out and use today?
lessons.jesus: Before his suffering, Jesus prayed to the Father, “I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do” (John 17:4). He is the most faithful steward of all, completing every disciple and every task the Father entrusted to him. He kept nothing for himself, but gave all the glory to the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, everything I have is entrusted to me by you. Forgive me for the times fear or comparison made me bury my gifts in the ground. I want to be your faithful steward, caring not about how much but about your pleasure. May I one day hear you say, “Well done, good and faithful servant.” In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down five “talents” the Lord has entrusted to you
Bring out a gift you have long kept buried and use it to serve someone
Use one of your talents to give practical help to one of “my 2”
lessons.noon: “Well done, good and faithful servant.” — Lord, right now I choose to be faithful to you.

lessons.title: Keeping Faith with My 2
lessons.theme: Keeping your word is the most practical way to love

v: Many men claim to be men of unfailing love, but who can find a faithful man?
But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.

lessons.still: Think back over the past month. What did you promise, and to whom? Which promises did you keep, and which did you forget? Don’t beat yourself up; honestly hand the list to the Lord: “Lord, help me to keep my word.”
teach: No one dares to cross a bridge that is sometimes there and sometimes not. A relationship is a bridge too, and trust is its pillars. We say, “Let’s have a meal sometime,” “I’ll pray for you,” “Leave it to me” — and if nothing ever comes of it, the pillars are eaten away one by one. This week we have moved from God’s faithfulness (Day 1), to faithfulness in little things (Day 2), to Daniel (Day 3), to being entrusted according to our ability (Day 4), and now to today.

Solomon sighed, “Many men claim to be men of unfailing love, but who can find a faithful man?” Fine words are easy; keeping promises is hard. Jesus said, “Let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’” There is no need to swear oaths for emphasis, because a faithful person’s ordinary words are already worth trusting.

Keeping faith with my 2 means letting them experience God’s reliability through me. Keeping faith also includes explaining honestly when I can’t do something, rather than quietly disappearing. Next week we will learn about gentleness, and gentleness needs the soil of trust — only the gentleness of someone who keeps their word puts people at ease.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. Breaking a promise may look like simply “forgetting something,” but in fact it wounds a person. The practice of 920 is to live out Christ’s faithfulness before each of my 2, so that our relationships become a witness to God’s kingdom.
q: Who is God? — God never breaks his word — what kind of security does that give you?
Who am I? — In the eyes of your 2, are you someone who keeps their word?
How shall I respond? — Which promise do you need to keep — or honestly explain — today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus told his disciples, “If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself.” He never promised lightly, and he never failed to keep a promise. His “Yes” is always “Yes”; all God’s promises are “Yes” in him (2 Corinthians 1:20).
lessons.pray: Faithful Lord, you have never once broken faith with me. Forgive me for so often promising lightly and forgetting easily. Help me to keep my word to the people around me, letting my yes be yes and my no be no. May my 2 experience your faithfulness through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Keep a promise you have been delaying for one of “my 2,” or honestly explain that you can’t
Don’t agree to things lightly today; when you do agree, write it down at once
Tomorrow (Saturday), share this week’s lessons in faithfulness with your spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.” — Lord, right now make my words as reliable as yours.
